title: Why Your Agent’s Brain Needs a Playbook: Practical Wins from Using Ontologies - Jesús Barrasa, Neo4j
talk_summary: Jesús Barrasa explains graph RAG: replacing a vector store with a knowledge graph, using an implementation-agnostic ontology as the schema to drive both graph construction and retrieval. The main practical trick is persisting the ontology in the graph so retrievers can dynamically consult it instead of hardcoding traversal logic.

takeaways.what_they_do: Persist the domain schema (ontology) as data in the graph, then have the retriever query the ontology to discover which relationships are 'contextualizing' and navigate only those, instead of hardcoding traversal logic.
Use one formal schema (ontology) to drive entity/relation extraction across both structured and unstructured pipelines, avoiding divergent JSON/Pydantic/natural-language schemas per pipeline.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this divergence is something that's uh you know not ideal to manage and what you want to do is have some kind of agnostic and and and general approach to to representing schemas

takeaways.what_they_do: Embed chunks as node properties in a vector index; on a vector hit, dereference back to the graph node and expand/filter/aggregate via graph relationships before passing context to the LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you find the the the vectors that are in proximity because these vectors are properties of a node we can dreference them and get back to the graph
